prompt: Write the checks that catch three clamp implementations which are all correct in the middle of the range and wrong at its edges. Complete isCorrect in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Boundary-value testing means probing lo, hi, just outside each end, and any degenerate range, because that is where off-by-one and inclusive/exclusive mistakes live. clamp(5, 0, 10) == 5 is true of all five implementations here, so it distinguishes nothing; clamp(0, 0, 10) exposes an exclusive lower bound, clamp(-3, 0, 10) exposes ends that were swapped, and clamp(7, 4, 4) exposes an implementation that gives up when the range has zero width. Writing the contract's examples down as checks turns fuzzy assumptions into decisions the code has to keep.
hints: A value in the middle of the range is returned unchanged by every implementation here. Test the value exactly equal to lo, and exactly equal to hi.
Test values on both sides of the range as well: something below lo must come back as lo, and something above hi must come back as hi -- not the other way round.
Do not skip the degenerate range where lo == hi, such as clamp(7, 4, 4) -> 4, and include a negative range like clamp(-20, -10, -1) -> -10.
